rows.label: The three quarterly reports and the annual report are filed by the issuer itself and can support all four selected modules. The three earnings releases describe the parent group, not the issuer, and must be labelled that way.
The issuer files its own statements, debt tables, maturity schedule and liquidity text in the annual report and each quarterly report.
The earnings releases report the parent group, whose cash, net income and debt differ from the issuer's.
October 2026 notes, a larger revolver and a covenant-definition amendment came after quarter-end and are described only in summary.
Covenant types are named, but covenant ratio values and governing definitions are not supplied.

Executed revolver credit agreement and its amendments (including the October 2026 third amendment), the indentures and the newbuild loan agreements are not supplied; the 10-K exhibit list names them as previously filed.

Covenant ratio values and definitions are not printed. The filings name a minimum liquidity test, a net funded debt to capitalization ratio and a loan to value ratio, and state compliance only. The third amendment “modified certain existing financial covenant definitions” (Q3 10-Q, page:12).
Press releases are parent-level (NCLH) and differ from issuer figures on cash, net income, debt and liquidity.
Total debt per the parent release and the issuer balance sheet are not reconciled in the supplied text.
Instrument-by-instrument debt at September 30, 2026 is not printed in the quarterly reports read; the full instrument table is at December 31, 2025 only.
Subsidiary guarantor names and the guarantor structure by note series are not supplied.
Events between October 29, 2026 and 2026-11-05 are not supplied.
The text extraction was not compared with the filed HTML or XBRL; tables are flattened across lines, so figures must be read against column headers.
Parent-level governance, ownership and strategy documents are not supplied beyond the releases.

Third, CP-0 did not record that the 10-K carries a springing maturity on the Revolving Loan Facility tied to November 17, 2026 (a contract date after the cutoff); see Covenants and facility terms. No earlier statement of CP-0 is withdrawn.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported base for the issuer, as filed, shows balance-sheet debt of 14,884.5 at Q3 2026 (current and long-term debt plus exchangeable notes at carrying value) against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of 2,700.1, which gives 5.51x, and 5.42x after deducting cash of 250.7. At FY2025 the same measures were 5.34x and 5.26x. The deterioration comes from both terms: debt carrying value rose from 14,583.4 while last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA slipped from 2,731.4, with the third quarter of 2026 at 936.7 against 1,019.4 a year earlier, down 8.1%. Reported net income is not a clean guide because other income of 200.1 in Q3 2026 (largely conversion-option gains) lifted net income to 631.9, above operating income of 624.2. Interest expense, net fell to 564.5 for 9M 2026 from 782.4, but the 9M 2025 figure included an extinguishment-related amount of 202.5, so the underlying fall is small. Cash interest is printed only for FY2025, so interim cash interest cover is Not supplied. Operating cash flow of 1,709.3 for 9M 2026 did not cover additions to property and equipment of 2,292.0, so growth is financed with new debt and export-credit loans; undrawn export-credit facilities of about 10.8 billion are stated against ship contracts of 19,421.2. Scheduled principal is 1,105.7 in 2027 and 4,134.3 in 2030, so the near-term profile is manageable and the 2030 wall is heavy. After the quarter, an 8.750% notes issue, a larger revolver and a covenant-definition amendment changed the picture, but only in summary form. Everything here is on the issuer's own perimeter; the parent's release shows different cash, net income, debt and leverage and is not mixed in.

facts.label: Debt by instrument
facts.text: - Issuer and guarantors as printed: NCLC is issuer of the exchangeable notes, with NCLH as guarantor: “pursuant to an indenture among NCLC, as issuer, NCLH, as guarantor, and U.S. Bank National Association, as trustee” (Q3 10-Q page:27). NCLC is borrower under the Revolving Loan Facility with subsidiary guarantors (Q3 10-Q page:29). The guarantors of each senior note series, and the security for each newbuild loan, are not stated in the debt table; “Approximately $15 billion of the net book value of our assets was pledged as collateral for certain of our debt as of September 30, 2026.” (Q3 10-Q page:42). - Naming trap: the 10-K labels the 5.875% notes due 2031 as the "2031 Notes", while the Q3 10-Q defines the new 8.750% notes due October 15, 2031 as the "2031 Notes" (Q3 10-Q page:11). They are different instruments. The 10-K table uses 2031 for the 5.875% issue only. - Exchangeable notes at September 30, 2026 (principal, carrying value, Q3 10-Q page:12): 2027 1.125% 192.0 and 188.3; 2027 2.5% 24.1 and 23.7; 2030 0.875% 353.9 and 306.2; 2030 0.750% 1,407.0 and 1,127.2. In May 2026 NCLC fixed cash settlement for exchanges of both 2027 series (Q3 10-Q page:12). - 2026 changes to the stack: Norwegian Luna export-credit term loan of €1.0 billion at 1.91% due February 25, 2038 (Q3 10-Q page:11); October 2026 issue of 950.0 of 8.750% senior unsecured notes due 2031, with proceeds used to “redeem all of the outstanding 6.125% senior notes due 2028” (Q3 10-Q page:11), to repay 380.0 of revolver borrowings and to prepay about 42.2 of export-credit facilities.

Under the Seventh ARCA, a loan to value ratio of less than 0.70 to 1.00, free liquidity of no less than 250 million at all times, an EBITDA to consolidated debt service ratio of at least 1.25 to 1.00 at each quarter-end unless free liquidity is at least 300 million, and a total net funded debt to total capitalization ratio (level not printed) (10-K page:41). - Reported compliance: “As of September 30, 2026, we were in compliance with all of our debt covenants.” (Q3 10-Q page:13). Reported covenant ratio values and headroom: Not supplied. The issuer's EBITDA, free liquidity and debt service definitions differ from the Adjusted EBITDA and balance-sheet debt computed here, so no headroom is inferred. - October 2026 amendment: the third amendment “also modified certain existing financial covenant definitions and the related collateral” (Q3 10-Q page:12). The text of the amendment is Not supplied. - Springing maturity, as stated in the 10-K: if on November 17, 2026 the 2027 1.125% or 2.5% exchangeable notes have not been repaid or refinanced with indebtedness maturing after April 23, 2030 and a liquidity test is not satisfied, the revolver maturity date becomes November 17, 2026 (10-K page:142). November 17, 2026 is after the cutoff and is a contract term, not an event. The Q3 10-Q does not restate this term, and whether the third amendment changed it is Not supplied. The liquidity test is not defined in the pages read. - Ratings, as printed: “Our Moody’s long-term issuer rating is B1, and our senior unsecured rating is B3.” (Q3 10-Q page:39); S&P Global issuer credit rating B+, revolver issue-level BB, senior unsecured B+ (same page).

facts.label: Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication
facts.text: - Leverage. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 fell 8.1% to 936.7 (Q3 10-Q page:34), while debt rose to 14,884.5. Mechanism: with a higher numerator and a lower denominator, leverage mechanically rises, and the quarter that carries most seasonal profit weakened. Implication: leverage on the issuer's own filings is 5.51x, above the 5.34x at FY2025; the company states net leverage on a parent basis of 5.5x, a consistent but non-identical measure. - Earnings quality. Evidence: Net Yield per Capacity Day fell to 319.65 from 341.89 in Q3 2026 and occupancy was roughly unchanged; the filing states the booked position “remains below its optimal range” (Q3 10-Q page:32). Mechanism: capacity grew (Capacity Days 6,766,454 against 6,417,724) while yield fell, so volume masks price. Implication: management describes about 125 million, 100 million and 100 million of run-rate savings as benefits to be realized over time (Q3 10-Q page:33); Adjusted Net Cruise Cost Excluding Fuel per Capacity Day was lower at 152.29 against 155.65, but the revenue side has not recovered, so earnings recovery is unproven. - Cash flow and funding model. Evidence: operating cash flow less additions to property and equipment is (582.7) for 9M 2026. Mechanism: newbuild deliveries are financed by export-credit loans at low fixed rates, such as the 1.91% Luna loan, but total debt grows with each delivery. Implication: deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth, not on free cash flow, until the newbuild cycle slows; committed ship payments of 19,421.2 stay ahead. - Liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: availability fell to 1.1 billion at Q3 2026, then October 2026 actions raised revolver commitments from about 2.5 billion to about 2.8 billion and repaid 380.0. Mechanism: the remaining 2027 exchangeable notes (216.2 principal in total, 212.5 carrying) are classified as current at September 30, 2026, and the 2030 wall of 4,134.3 follows. Implication: near-term liquidity looks adequate on the filings, but the springing-maturity term and amended covenants need the agreements before comfort. - Perimeter. The earnings releases describe the parent, whose cash, net income and debt differ from the issuer's. Implication: credit metrics for this issuer must come from the 10-K and 10-Qs.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The credit-relevant structure is simple but concentrated. NCLC is the operating cruise subsidiary of a listed parent, owns three brands (Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises) and ships them in one reportable segment, so there is no segment to diversify away from a weak brand. NCLH owns all NCLC ordinary shares, guarantees NCLC's exchangeable notes, receives NCLC's cash only subject to debt-agreement restrictions, and its equity price drives the value of the exchange option inside those notes. The operating model is a high fixed-cost, seasonal business that collects cash ahead of sailing: advance ticket sales are the main working capital funding and are partly refundable, so booking strength is the lead indicator of liquidity. Capital intensity is high and rising: the filings list 13 effective newbuild contracts, export-credit financing for roughly four fifths of most contracts, and three effective contracts that are not yet financed. In 2026 the company is actively reshaping the fleet, with long-term charters and sales of older ships, a new chief executive from February 2026, cost-saving programs and a booked position that management says remains below its optimal range. There is no sponsor, no merger and no dividend recapitalisation in the sources. The transaction content is therefore financing and fleet transactions, which are dated and described below. The sources lack governance papers for the issuer (the annual report uses a reduced disclosure format), the credit agreements, and any statement of how NCLH's strategy would be funded at NCLC. Those gaps limit, but do not block, the downstream work.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Completed in FY2025 (10-K page:141 to page:146): in January 2025 NCLC issued senior unsecured notes due 2032 and amended and restated the Revolving Loan Facility (the Seventh ARCA); in April 2025 it exchanged part of its 2025 exchangeable notes into new 2030 0.875% Exchangeable Notes; in June 2025 it amended the facility to raise commitments to approximately 2.5 billion; in September 2025 it issued 2030 0.750% Exchangeable Notes, 5.875% senior unsecured notes due 2031 and 6.250% notes due 2033 and used the exchangeable proceeds, together with the proceeds of an NCLH equity offering and cash, to repurchase most of the 2027 exchangeable notes. NCLH's equity offerings in April and September 2025 supplied cash used in those exchange and repurchase steps. Newbuild export-credit loans for Norwegian Aqua (March 2025) and Oceania Allura (July 2025) were also drawn.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: NCL Corporation Ltd. is a leveraged but liquid cruise credit whose deleveraging has stalled: net debt is 5.42x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, up from 5.26x at FY2025. The strongest support is liquidity of about USD 1,350.7 million (cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million), a revolver upsized in October 2026 and, on the December 31, 2025 debt table and the 2026 events described, no senior unsecured note maturity before 2029. The weakest point is cash generation: operating cash flow less additions to property and equipment was negative USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 while Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell 8.1%. What decides the outcome is whether 2027 yield recovers and how the November 17, 2026 springing maturity and the amended covenants resolve; neither amendment text is supplied.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

citations.quote: NCL Corporation Ltd. is a leveraged but liquid cruise credit whose deleveraging has stalled: net debt is 5.42x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, up from 5.26x at FY2025. The strongest support is liquidity of about USD 1,350.7 million (cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million), a revolver upsized in October 2026 and, on the December 31, 2025 debt table and the 2026 events described, no senior unsecured note maturity before 2029. The weakest point is cash generation: operating cash flow less additions to property and equipment was negative USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 while Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell 8.1%. What decides the outcome is whether 2027 yield recovers and how the November 17, 2026 springing maturity and the amended covenants resolve; neither amendment text is supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage is high and has risen. NCLC carried balance-sheet debt of USD 14,884.5 million at September 30, 2026 against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,700.1 million, which is 5.51x, and 5.42x net of USD 250.7 million of cash; at FY2025 the figures were 5.34x and 5.26x on USD 2,731.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 was USD 936.7 million against USD 1,019.4 million, with Net Yield per Capacity Day at USD 319.65 against USD 341.89, so volume is growing while price per unit falls [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:34]. The parent states net leverage of 5.5x on its own perimeter; that is a consistent but separate measure and is not used here (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, near-term liquidity is adequate on the issuer's own filings. At September 30, 2026 NCLC had cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million, which the filing totals as liquidity of about USD 1.4 billion [Q3 10-Q page:6]. Scheduled principal is USD 238.6 million for the rest of 2026 and USD 1,105.7 million in 2027 [CP-1]. In October 2026 NCLC issued USD 950.0 million of 8.750% senior unsecured notes due 2031, repaid USD 380.0 million of revolver borrowings, redeemed the 6.125% notes due 2028 and raised revolver commitments from about USD 2.5 billion to about USD 2.8 billion, which on printed figures lifts revolver availability to about USD 1,780 million (calculated); the parent's own pro forma figure is USD 1.8 billion and is parent-level [Q3 10-Q page:12; Q3 release page:3].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, the revolver carries a springing maturity that falls 12 days after the as-of date. The 10-K states that if on November 17, 2026 the 2027 1.125% or 2.5% exchangeable notes have not been repaid or refinanced with debt maturing after April 23, 2030 and a liquidity test is not satisfied, the commitments and loans mature on November 17, 2026 [10-K page:142]. Both series mature on February 15, 2027 and total USD 216.2 million of principal; NCLC states it expects to repay them in cash or refinance before maturity, and held USD 250.7 million of cash [Q3 10-Q page:38]. The liquidity test is not defined in the pages read, the Q3 10-Q does not restate the clause, and the October 2026 third amendment may have changed it. This is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding, but it is the most time-sensitive item because the facility is the main liquidity backstop (Insufficient Information).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, capital commitments are large, mostly financed and partly open. Non-cancelable ship contracts total USD 19,421.2 million for 13 effective ships, with committed undrawn export-credit facilities of about USD 10.8 billion funding about 80% of most contracts; three effective contracts (Oceania Sonata Class 3 in 2032, Regent Prestige Class 3 in 2033 and Oceania Sonata Class 4 in 2035) are “Contract effective, but not yet financed” [Q3 10-Q page:20, page:41 and page:42]. Anticipated ship construction and growth spending is USD 1.1 billion for the rest of 2026, USD 3.1 billion in 2027 and USD 1.8 billion in 2028, against export-credit funding of USD 0.6 billion, USD 2.0 billion and USD 1.3 billion [Q3 10-Q page:40]. The unfunded part in 2027, USD 1.1 billion, plus scheduled principal of USD 1,105.7 million is USD 2,205.7 million, which is 1.02x last-twelve-months operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million (calculated, from printed rounded figures). Little room is left for deleveraging from internally generated cash in 2027 (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fifth, the debt stack is long-dated and mostly fixed rate, which supports debt service but concentrates maturities. At September 30, 2026, 88% of debt was fixed and 12% variable, and a one percentage point rise in SOFR would raise annual interest expense by about USD 18.2 million [Q3 10-Q page:43]. Scheduled principal is USD 1,346.1 million in 2028, USD 1,370.0 million in 2029 and USD 4,134.3 million in 2030, which together are 44.2% of the USD 15,498.0 million total, and 2030 alone is 26.7% (calculated) [CP-1]. The October 2026 actions change those buckets: if the full USD 525.0 million of 6.125% notes was outstanding, 2028 falls to about USD 821.1 million; if the revolver sits in the 2030 bucket, repaying USD 380.0 million takes 2030 to about USD 3,754.3 million; and 2031 rises to about USD 2,825.1 million with the new notes (calculated, illustrative; the USD 42.2 million of export-credit prepayment is not allocated). The 2030 maturities include the revolver (stated maturity January 22, 2030), two exchangeable series and the 6.25% senior unsecured notes [10-K page:139 and page:142]. Interest expense, net fell to USD 564.5 million for nine months 2026 from USD 782.4 million, but about USD 202.5 million of the earlier amount was extinguishment loss, so the underlying fall was 2.7% (calculated) [CP-1].

facts.text: Sixth, currency exposure is large on the capital side. Euro-denominated ship payments not hedged were EUR 14.1 billion (USD 16.0 billion) and unhedged euro debt about EUR 2.1 billion (USD 2.4 billion); a 10% change in the euro would change the dollar value of the unhedged payments by USD 1.6 billion and of the unhedged debt principal by USD 237.7 million [Q3 10-Q page:44]. The payments fall due over many years, so the effect on cash is gradual, but it moves the dollar cost of commitments that the export-credit loans only partly fund (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.text: Seventh, covenant headroom cannot be measured. The 10-K names a loan to value ratio below 0.70 to 1.00, free liquidity of at least USD 250 million at all times, an EBITDA to consolidated debt service ratio of at least 1.25 to 1.00 unless free liquidity is at least USD 300 million, and a net funded debt to total capitalization ratio whose level is not printed [10-K page:41]. Compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 [Q3 10-Q page:13], but no ratio values are printed. Cash alone was USD 179.2 million at March 31, 2026 and USD 212.3 million at June 30, 2026, below the USD 250 million level, so the free-liquidity definition must count undrawn revolver capacity or similar sources; the definition is not supplied (Insufficient Information and Analyst Interpretation). The October 2026 amendment “also modified certain existing financial covenant definitions and the related collateral” [Q3 10-Q page:12].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Eighth, the issuer sits under a parent and the exchangeable notes link the two. NCLH owns all NCLC shares, guarantees the exchangeable notes on a senior unsecured basis, and the notes exchange into NCLH shares with cash up to principal and cash or shares for any excess [10-K page:144; CP-1A]. NCLH passed equity proceeds to NCLC in 2025 and no distribution to the parent appears in the periods read [CP-1A]. The Havana Docks matter names NCLH as defendant, was remanded to the Eleventh Circuit in June 2026 and is “reasonably possible but not probable” with no liability recorded; whether NCLC bears it is not stated [Q3 10-Q page:22] (Insufficient Information).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and near-term maturities: cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million against USD 238.6 million of scheduled principal for the rest of 2026, with the revolver upsized after quarter-end (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Funding model: most new ships are financed by long-dated fixed-rate export-credit loans, such as the 1.91% term loan maturing February 25, 2038 for Norwegian Luna, and about USD 10.8 billion of committed undrawn facilities remain (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:42). (3) Fixed-rate profile: 88% of debt is fixed, so base-rate moves affect a small part of interest cost (Documentary Fact; Q3 10-Q page:43). (4) Parent support and no leakage: NCLH contributed equity proceeds in 2025 and no distributions to the parent appear in the periods read (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (5) Operating cash flow of USD 1,709.3 million for nine months 2026 and seasonally strong third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.8% (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (6) Management cost and fleet actions, including run-rate savings programs and ship charters and sales, are described and under way, but are Management Language until they show in results (Management Language; CP-1A).

facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) Leverage of 5.51x total and 5.42x net, higher than at FY2025 (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Negative post-capex cash flow of USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 and growth spending financed by debt (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (3) Earnings and yield softness: Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA down 8.1%, Net Yield lower, and a booked position that management says remains below its optimal range (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (4) Springing revolver maturity on November 17, 2026 with an undefined liquidity test (Insufficient Information; 10-K page:142). (5) Concentrated maturities in 2030 and an unfinanced part of the newbuild program (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:41). (7) Demand concentration: about 84% of revenue from U.S.-sourced guests and customer deposits that are partly refundable (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (8) Evidence gaps: no agreements, no covenant values, a reduced-disclosure annual report and a perimeter difference between the issuer's filings and the parent's releases (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A).

Cash of 250.7 and revolver availability of about 1,100 compare with scheduled principal of 238.6 for the rest of 2026.
The revolver can mature on November 17, 2026, 12 days after the as-of date, unless the 2027 exchangeable notes are repaid or refinanced or a liquidity test is met.
Committed ship payments are 19,421.2, with about 10,800 of export-credit facilities and three effective contracts not yet financed.
Scheduled principal is 1,105.7 in 2027 and 4,134.3 in 2030.

Fundamental view: high leverage with adequate near-term liquidity, softening earnings, negative post-capex cash flow, long-dated mostly fixed-rate export-credit funding and an unresolved revolver springing-maturity test. Not a rating and not a recommendation.

### Financial base view

The reported base for the issuer, as filed, shows balance-sheet debt of 14,884.5 at Q3 2026 (current and long-term debt plus exchangeable notes at carrying value) against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of 2,700.1, which gives 5.51x, and 5.42x after deducting cash of 250.7. At FY2025 the same measures were 5.34x and 5.26x. The deterioration comes from both terms: debt carrying value rose from 14,583.4 while last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA slipped from 2,731.4, with the third quarter of 2026 at 936.7 against 1,019.4 a year earlier, down 8.1%. Reported net income is not a clean guide because other income of 200.1 in Q3 2026 (largely conversion-option gains) lifted net income to 631.9, above operating income of 624.2. Interest expense, net fell to 564.5 for 9M 2026 from 782.4, but the 9M 2025 figure included an extinguishment-related amount of 202.5, so the underlying fall is small. Cash interest is printed only for FY2025, so interim cash interest cover is Not supplied. Operating cash flow of 1,709.3 for 9M 2026 did not cover additions to property and equipment of 2,292.0, so growth is financed with new debt and export-credit loans; undrawn export-credit facilities of about 10.8 billion are stated against ship contracts of 19,421.2. Scheduled principal is 1,105.7 in 2027 and 4,134.3 in 2030, so the near-term profile is manageable and the 2030 wall is heavy. After the quarter, an 8.750% notes issue, a larger revolver and a covenant-definition amendment changed the picture, but only in summary form. Everything here is on the issuer's own perimeter; the parent's release shows different cash, net income, debt and leverage and is not mixed in.

### Covenants and facility terms

- Covenant types, from the 10-K: “Certain of our debt facilities include maintenance and financial covenants.” (10-K page:41). Under the Seventh ARCA, a loan to value ratio of less than 0.70 to 1.00, free liquidity of no less than 250 million at all times, an EBITDA to consolidated debt service ratio of at least 1.25 to 1.00 at each quarter-end unless free liquidity is at least 300 million, and a total net funded debt to total capitalization ratio (level not printed) (10-K page:41).

- Reported compliance: “As of September 30, 2026, we were in compliance with all of our debt covenants.” (Q3 10-Q page:13). Reported covenant ratio values and headroom: Not supplied. The issuer's EBITDA, free liquidity and debt service definitions differ from the Adjusted EBITDA and balance-sheet debt computed here, so no headroom is inferred.
- October 2026 amendment: the third amendment “also modified certain existing financial covenant definitions and the related collateral” (Q3 10-Q page:12). The text of the amendment is Not supplied.

- Springing maturity, as stated in the 10-K: if on November 17, 2026 the 2027 1.125% or 2.5% exchangeable notes have not been repaid or refinanced with indebtedness maturing after April 23, 2030 and a liquidity test is not satisfied, the revolver maturity date becomes November 17, 2026 (10-K page:142). November 17, 2026 is after the cutoff and is a contract term, not an event. The Q3 10-Q does not restate this term, and whether the third amendment changed it is Not supplied. The liquidity test is not defined in the pages read.

- Ratings, as printed: “Our Moody’s long-term issuer rating is B1, and our senior unsecured rating is B3.” (Q3 10-Q page:39); S&P Global issuer credit rating B+, revolver issue-level BB, senior unsecured B+ (same page).
### Events, comparability and subsequent events
- Q1 2026: delivery of Norwegian Luna and its €1.0 billion export-credit loan (Q1 10-Q page:9).

- Q2 2026: cash settlement fixed for the 2027 exchangeable notes (May 2026, Q2 10-Q page:10); memorandum of agreement for the sale of Oceania Sirena in July 2026, a subsequent event at that report date (Q2 10-Q page:21 to page:22).

- Q3 2026: Oceania Sirena sold in September 2026, with a loss on disposal of 16.8 (Q3 10-Q page:7) and ship sale proceeds of 105.0 for 9M 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:3); a bareboat charter for Norwegian Sky started in September 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:10). Restructuring costs of 22.4 and professional advisory fees of 5.4 for 9M 2026 are added back in Adjusted EBITDA (Q3 10-Q page:36). Q3 2026 other income of 200.1 reverses a (134.4) loss a year earlier (Q3 10-Q page:2).

- After September 30, 2026 and before the cutoff: the 950.0 notes issue and revolver third amendment (Q3 10-Q page:11 to page:12) and a memorandum of agreement for the sale of Oceania Insignia, closing September 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:24). The parent's release states pro forma liquidity of 2.1 billion, parent-level and management-prepared (Q3 release page:3).

- Comparability: revenue by destination shows Asia-Pacific revenue of 12.4 in Q3 2026 against 124.8, so mix shifts between years are large. FY2025 interest expense, net includes about 202.5 of extinguishment losses (10-K page:150).
### Interpretation: data to risk to credit implication

- Leverage. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 fell 8.1% to 936.7 (Q3 10-Q page:34), while debt rose to 14,884.5. Mechanism: with a higher numerator and a lower denominator, leverage mechanically rises, and the quarter that carries most seasonal profit weakened. Implication: leverage on the issuer's own filings is 5.51x, above the 5.34x at FY2025; the company states net leverage on a parent basis of 5.5x, a consistent but non-identical measure.

- Earnings quality. Evidence: Net Yield per Capacity Day fell to 319.65 from 341.89 in Q3 2026 and occupancy was roughly unchanged; the filing states the booked position “remains below its optimal range” (Q3 10-Q page:32). Mechanism: capacity grew (Capacity Days 6,766,454 against 6,417,724) while yield fell, so volume masks price. Implication: management describes about 125 million, 100 million and 100 million of run-rate savings as benefits to be realized over time (Q3 10-Q page:33); Adjusted Net Cruise Cost Excluding Fuel per Capacity Day was lower at 152.29 against 155.65, but the revenue side has not recovered, so earnings recovery is unproven.

- Cash flow and funding model. Evidence: operating cash flow less additions to property and equipment is (582.7) for 9M 2026. Mechanism: newbuild deliveries are financed by export-credit loans at low fixed rates, such as the 1.91% Luna loan, but total debt grows with each delivery. Implication: deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth, not on free cash flow, until the newbuild cycle slows; committed ship payments of 19,421.2 stay ahead.

- Liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: availability fell to 1.1 billion at Q3 2026, then October 2026 actions raised revolver commitments from about 2.5 billion to about 2.8 billion and repaid 380.0. Mechanism: the remaining 2027 exchangeable notes (216.2 principal in total, 212.5 carrying) are classified as current at September 30, 2026, and the 2030 wall of 4,134.3 follows. Implication: near-term liquidity looks adequate on the filings, but the springing-maturity term and amended covenants need the agreements before comfort.
- Perimeter. The earnings releases describe the parent, whose cash, net income and debt differ from the issuer's. Implication: credit metrics for this issuer must come from the 10-K and 10-Qs.
## Calculations
All inputs are US$ thousands as printed, converted to US$m by dividing by 1,000.
### LTM Adjusted EBITDA
LTM = FY2025 + year-to-date current − year-to-date prior.
### LTM and discrete income and cash flow lines
- Depreciation and amortization LTM: 1,078,755 + 819,624 − 725,889 = 1,172,490.
- Q3 2026 change in Adjusted EBITDA: 936,702 / 1,019,351 − 1 = −8.1% (matches the 10-Q statement of an 8.1% decrease). 9M 2026 revenue change: 7,918,528 / 7,583,192 − 1 = 4.4%.
### Debt and leverage ratios

- Cash interest cover FY2025: 2,731,377 / 952,000 = 2.87; excluding early redemption premium 162,374: 2,731,377 / (952,000 − 162,374) = 2,731,377 / 789,626 = 3.46. Inputs: 10-K page:169 (952.0 as printed in US$ millions, converted to thousands) and 10-K page:123 (premium).
- Operating lease liabilities: 34,192 + 906,131 = 940,323 (Q3 10-Q page:10).
### Liquidity

- Reported liquidity is printed rounded: Q3 2026 about 1.4 billion = cash 250.7 + 1.1 billion available under the Revolving Loan Facility (Q3 10-Q page:6 and page:38). Sum of printed components 250.7 + 1,100 = 1,350.7, consistent with the rounded 1.4 billion. A revolver drawn amount is not printed at Q3 2026; it is therefore Not supplied (the 10-K prints 1,100.0 drawn at December 31, 2025, 10-K page:139).

- Consistency check on the parent's pro forma: printed availability 1.1 billion + commitment increase of about 0.3 billion (about 2.5 to about 2.8) + 380.0 repaid is about 1.78 billion, in line with the parent's stated 1.8 billion; this checks the arithmetic only and is not an issuer figure.
### Underlying interest change

- 9M 2025 interest expense, net 782,390 includes extinguishment and modification of debt of 202,525 (Q3 10-Q page:35 Adjusted Net Income table). Excluding it: 782,390 − 202,525 = 579,865. 9M 2026 564,473 / 579,865 − 1 = −2.7%. Without the exclusion the reported change is 564,473 / 782,390 − 1 = −27.9%.
### Tie-outs
- Debt table: the 29 carrying values in Debt by instrument add to 14,583,441, equal to the 10-K total debt (10-K page:140).

- Unreconciled: the parent's total debt of 15,086.5 and net debt of 14,830.0 (Q3 release page:18) differ from the issuer's 14,884.5 and 14,633.8; the difference is not explained in the supplied text and is not bridged.
## Gaps

## Next module

CP-1A should run next on the business, fleet, ownership and transaction context (ship sales and charters, the October 2026 financing and the parent relationship). CP-2 and CP-5 follow. Carry forward these limits: the issuer-only perimeter, the missing covenant values and agreements, the November 17, 2026 springing-maturity term, the absence of an instrument table at September 30, 2026, and the two different instruments labelled "2031 Notes".

| The business is a three-brand cruise operator with seasonal demand, about 84% U.S.-sourced guests and advance ticket sales funding working capital. | Cash conversion depends on bookings and customer deposits, which are partly refundable. | Medium |

| Thirteen effective newbuild contracts carry large commitments, and three effective contracts are not yet financed. | Funding of later deliveries is not secured, and capital spending will keep debt high. | Medium |

| Older ships are being chartered or sold, and October 2026 brought a new notes issue and a larger revolver. | Asset sales and refinancing support liquidity, but loss of sold ships reduces the collateral and earnings base. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The credit-relevant structure is simple but concentrated. NCLC is the operating cruise subsidiary of a listed parent, owns three brands (Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises) and ships them in one reportable segment, so there is no segment to diversify away from a weak brand. NCLH owns all NCLC ordinary shares, guarantees NCLC's exchangeable notes, receives NCLC's cash only subject to debt-agreement restrictions, and its equity price drives the value of the exchange option inside those notes. The operating model is a high fixed-cost, seasonal business that collects cash ahead of sailing: advance ticket sales are the main working capital funding and are partly refundable, so booking strength is the lead indicator of liquidity. Capital intensity is high and rising: the filings list 13 effective newbuild contracts, export-credit financing for roughly four fifths of most contracts, and three effective contracts that are not yet financed. In 2026 the company is actively reshaping the fleet, with long-term charters and sales of older ships, a new chief executive from February 2026, cost-saving programs and a booked position that management says remains below its optimal range. There is no sponsor, no merger and no dividend recapitalisation in the sources. The transaction content is therefore financing and fleet transactions, which are dated and described below. The sources lack governance papers for the issuer (the annual report uses a reduced disclosure format), the credit agreements, and any statement of how NCLH's strategy would be funded at NCLC. Those gaps limit, but do not block, the downstream work.

| Area | Fact | Category | Locator | Credit relevance |

| Core activity | “We are a leading global cruise company, which operates the Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises brands.” At September 30, 2026 the combined fleet was 33 ships with approximately 72,000 Berths. | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:5 | Revenue rests on discretionary leisure travel across three price tiers. |

| Fleet movement | The fleet was 34 ships with approximately 71,400 Berths at December 31, 2025; the decrease since June 30, 2026 is due to Norwegian Sky and Oceania Regatta commencing long-term charters to third parties. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:9; Q3 10-Q page:5 | Chartered-out ships leave the operated fleet and the earnings base, but may be retained as assets. |

| Segment | The business has a single reportable segment; each brand is a business for which discrete information is available. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:128 | No segment diversification inside the issuer. |

| Revenue model | Passenger ticket revenue (accommodation, meals, entertainment, taxes and port fees, air and land packages) and onboard and other revenue (casino, beverage, shore excursions, specialty dining, retail, spa, Wi-Fi and long-term ship charters). Nine months 2026 revenue was 5,217.8 passenger ticket and 2,700.7 onboard and other (US$m). | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:2 and page:31 | Onboard revenue carries direct costs and depends on guest spending on board. |

| Geography and customers | “Our revenue attributable to U.S.-sourced guests has approximated 84% of total revenue over the preceding three fiscal years.” is the concentration disclosed; revenue by destination for nine months 2026 is North America 4,991.7, Europe 2,104.9, Asia-Pacific 588.2 and Other 233.7 against 4,200.7, 2,386.5, 763.6 and 232.5 for nine months 2025 (US$m). | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:9 | A single source market dominates demand; Europe and Asia-Pacific revenue fell year on year while North America rose. |

| Pricing and inclusions | Norwegian prices typically include meals in certain dining facilities and many onboard activities; Oceania Cruises prices include specialty dining, Wi-Fi, laundry and gratuities; Regent fares are all-inclusive including unlimited shore excursions. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 and page:10 | Brand positioning ranges from mass-premium to luxury; pricing is the main yield lever. |

| Seasonality | “Our operations are seasonal and results for interim periods are not necessarily indicative of the results for the entire fiscal year.” Demand is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere summer. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 | The third quarter carries most profit; interim leverage and liquidity swing seasonally. |

| Cost structure | Largest operating costs are payroll and related (including a third-party crew services contract), fuel, airfare, food and beverage, advertising and travel advisor services; fuel was approximately 48% hedged for the remainder of 2026. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13; Q3 10-Q page:33 | Fuel and payroll are the volatile cost lines; hedging covers part of the fuel risk only. |

| Working capital | “As of December 31, 2025, we had a working capital deficit of $4.4 billion” including $3.2 billion of advance ticket sales, which management describes as substantially like deferred revenue. | Management Language | 10-K page:84 | Customer deposits fund operations and are partly refundable, so a booking slowdown drains cash. |

| Private destinations | The company operates Great Stirrup Cay in The Bahamas and Harvest Caye in Belize; the Great Tides Waterpark at Great Stirrup Cay opened in September 2026. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:10; Q3 10-Q page:32 | Owned destinations support itineraries and onboard spend; their costs are capital items. |

| Competition | Primary competitors include Carnival and Royal Caribbean, as well as MSC Cruises, Viking Ocean Cruises and Virgin Voyages, and land-based vacation alternatives. | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 | Industry capacity and pricing are set by larger peers. |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction or leveraged buyout in the sources, and the context supplies no deal terms, so the transaction content is financing and fleet activity, with each item below at its stated status.

Completed in FY2025 (10-K page:141 to page:146): in January 2025 NCLC issued senior unsecured notes due 2032 and amended and restated the Revolving Loan Facility (the Seventh ARCA); in April 2025 it exchanged part of its 2025 exchangeable notes into new 2030 0.875% Exchangeable Notes; in June 2025 it amended the facility to raise commitments to approximately 2.5 billion; in September 2025 it issued 2030 0.750% Exchangeable Notes, 5.875% senior unsecured notes due 2031 and 6.250% notes due 2033 and used the exchangeable proceeds, together with the proceeds of an NCLH equity offering and cash, to repurchase most of the 2027 exchangeable notes. NCLH's equity offerings in April and September 2025 supplied cash used in those exchange and repurchase steps. Newbuild export-credit loans for Norwegian Aqua (March 2025) and Oceania Allura (July 2025) were also drawn.

Completed in 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:9; Q2 10-Q page:10; Q3 10-Q page:11 and page:32): delivery of Norwegian Luna in March 2026 with a €1.0 billion export-credit term loan at 1.91% maturing February 25, 2038; an irrevocable election in May 2026 to settle exchanges of both 2027 exchangeable note series in cash; the sale of Oceania Sirena in September 2026 with continued operation under a bareboat charter through spring 2028; the start of the Norwegian Sky bareboat charter in September 2026; and the start of a two-year time charter for Oceania Regatta in September 2026.

Executed and pending: a nine-year lease of Seven Seas Navigator executed in March 2026, commencing December 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:10); a ten-year bareboat charter for Norwegian Sun expected to commence in late 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:32); and a memorandum of agreement for the sale of Oceania Insignia, with closing in September 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:24). The sale price and the buyer are Not supplied.

New debt after the quarter and before the cutoff: on October 15, 2026 NCLC issued 950.0 of 8.750% senior unsecured notes due October 15, 2031, used with cash on hand to redeem all of the outstanding 6.125% senior notes due 2028, repay 380.0 of revolver borrowings and prepay about 42.2 of export-credit facilities, and entered into a third amendment that raised Revolving Loan Facility commitments from approximately 2.5 billion to approximately 2.8 billion and modified certain financial covenant definitions and collateral (Q3 10-Q page:11 to page:12; Q3 release page:1). The parent release adds a pro forma liquidity figure of 2.1 billion at September 30, 2026 (Q3 release page:3), which is parent-level and management-prepared. The indenture and amendment texts are Not supplied. Merger-related debt does not exist in the sources; the one liquidity effect described for the issuer is the October 2026 refinancing.

## Findings
### Reader summary

### Credit view

NCL Corporation Ltd. is a leveraged but liquid cruise credit whose deleveraging has stalled: net debt is 5.42x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, up from 5.26x at FY2025. The strongest support is liquidity of about USD 1,350.7 million (cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million), a revolver upsized in October 2026 and, on the December 31, 2025 debt table and the 2026 events described, no senior unsecured note maturity before 2029. The weakest point is cash generation: operating cash flow less additions to property and equipment was negative USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 while Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell 8.1%. What decides the outcome is whether 2027 yield recovers and how the November 17, 2026 springing maturity and the amended covenants resolve; neither amendment text is supplied.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental view: high leverage with adequate near-term liquidity, softening earnings, negative post-capex cash flow, long-dated mostly fixed-rate export-credit funding and an unresolved revolver springing-maturity test. Not a rating and not a recommendation. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium (below High because covenant values, agreements and the October 2026 amendment text are not supplied) | CP-1 leverage, liquidity, maturity and cash flow figures; CP-1A parent linkage, newbuild and fleet rows; Q3 10-Q market-risk and commitments pages |
### Key findings

First, leverage is high and has risen. NCLC carried balance-sheet debt of USD 14,884.5 million at September 30, 2026 against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,700.1 million, which is 5.51x, and 5.42x net of USD 250.7 million of cash; at FY2025 the figures were 5.34x and 5.26x on USD 2,731.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 was USD 936.7 million against USD 1,019.4 million, with Net Yield per Capacity Day at USD 319.65 against USD 341.89, so volume is growing while price per unit falls [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:34]. The parent states net leverage of 5.5x on its own perimeter; that is a consistent but separate measure and is not used here (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

Second, near-term liquidity is adequate on the issuer's own filings. At September 30, 2026 NCLC had cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million, which the filing totals as liquidity of about USD 1.4 billion [Q3 10-Q page:6]. Scheduled principal is USD 238.6 million for the rest of 2026 and USD 1,105.7 million in 2027 [CP-1]. In October 2026 NCLC issued USD 950.0 million of 8.750% senior unsecured notes due 2031, repaid USD 380.0 million of revolver borrowings, redeemed the 6.125% notes due 2028 and raised revolver commitments from about USD 2.5 billion to about USD 2.8 billion, which on printed figures lifts revolver availability to about USD 1,780 million (calculated); the parent's own pro forma figure is USD 1.8 billion and is parent-level [Q3 10-Q page:12; Q3 release page:3].

Third, the revolver carries a springing maturity that falls 12 days after the as-of date. The 10-K states that if on November 17, 2026 the 2027 1.125% or 2.5% exchangeable notes have not been repaid or refinanced with debt maturing after April 23, 2030 and a liquidity test is not satisfied, the commitments and loans mature on November 17, 2026 [10-K page:142]. Both series mature on February 15, 2027 and total USD 216.2 million of principal; NCLC states it expects to repay them in cash or refinance before maturity, and held USD 250.7 million of cash [Q3 10-Q page:38]. The liquidity test is not defined in the pages read, the Q3 10-Q does not restate the clause, and the October 2026 third amendment may have changed it. This is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding, but it is the most time-sensitive item because the facility is the main liquidity backstop (Insufficient Information).

Fourth, capital commitments are large, mostly financed and partly open. Non-cancelable ship contracts total USD 19,421.2 million for 13 effective ships, with committed undrawn export-credit facilities of about USD 10.8 billion funding about 80% of most contracts; three effective contracts (Oceania Sonata Class 3 in 2032, Regent Prestige Class 3 in 2033 and Oceania Sonata Class 4 in 2035) are “Contract effective, but not yet financed” [Q3 10-Q page:20, page:41 and page:42]. Anticipated ship construction and growth spending is USD 1.1 billion for the rest of 2026, USD 3.1 billion in 2027 and USD 1.8 billion in 2028, against export-credit funding of USD 0.6 billion, USD 2.0 billion and USD 1.3 billion [Q3 10-Q page:40]. The unfunded part in 2027, USD 1.1 billion, plus scheduled principal of USD 1,105.7 million is USD 2,205.7 million, which is 1.02x last-twelve-months operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million (calculated, from printed rounded figures). Little room is left for deleveraging from internally generated cash in 2027 (Analyst Interpretation).

Fifth, the debt stack is long-dated and mostly fixed rate, which supports debt service but concentrates maturities. At September 30, 2026, 88% of debt was fixed and 12% variable, and a one percentage point rise in SOFR would raise annual interest expense by about USD 18.2 million [Q3 10-Q page:43]. Scheduled principal is USD 1,346.1 million in 2028, USD 1,370.0 million in 2029 and USD 4,134.3 million in 2030, which together are 44.2% of the USD 15,498.0 million total, and 2030 alone is 26.7% (calculated) [CP-1]. The October 2026 actions change those buckets: if the full USD 525.0 million of 6.125% notes was outstanding, 2028 falls to about USD 821.1 million; if the revolver sits in the 2030 bucket, repaying USD 380.0 million takes 2030 to about USD 3,754.3 million; and 2031 rises to about USD 2,825.1 million with the new notes (calculated, illustrative; the USD 42.2 million of export-credit prepayment is not allocated). The 2030 maturities include the revolver (stated maturity January 22, 2030), two exchangeable series and the 6.25% senior unsecured notes [10-K page:139 and page:142]. Interest expense, net fell to USD 564.5 million for nine months 2026 from USD 782.4 million, but about USD 202.5 million of the earlier amount was extinguishment loss, so the underlying fall was 2.7% (calculated) [CP-1].

Sixth, currency exposure is large on the capital side. Euro-denominated ship payments not hedged were EUR 14.1 billion (USD 16.0 billion) and unhedged euro debt about EUR 2.1 billion (USD 2.4 billion); a 10% change in the euro would change the dollar value of the unhedged payments by USD 1.6 billion and of the unhedged debt principal by USD 237.7 million [Q3 10-Q page:44]. The payments fall due over many years, so the effect on cash is gradual, but it moves the dollar cost of commitments that the export-credit loans only partly fund (Analyst Interpretation).

Seventh, covenant headroom cannot be measured. The 10-K names a loan to value ratio below 0.70 to 1.00, free liquidity of at least USD 250 million at all times, an EBITDA to consolidated debt service ratio of at least 1.25 to 1.00 unless free liquidity is at least USD 300 million, and a net funded debt to total capitalization ratio whose level is not printed [10-K page:41]. Compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 [Q3 10-Q page:13], but no ratio values are printed. Cash alone was USD 179.2 million at March 31, 2026 and USD 212.3 million at June 30, 2026, below the USD 250 million level, so the free-liquidity definition must count undrawn revolver capacity or similar sources; the definition is not supplied (Insufficient Information and Analyst Interpretation). The October 2026 amendment “also modified certain existing financial covenant definitions and the related collateral” [Q3 10-Q page:12].

Eighth, the issuer sits under a parent and the exchangeable notes link the two. NCLH owns all NCLC shares, guarantees the exchangeable notes on a senior unsecured basis, and the notes exchange into NCLH shares with cash up to principal and cash or shares for any excess [10-K page:144; CP-1A]. NCLH passed equity proceeds to NCLC in 2025 and no distribution to the parent appears in the periods read [CP-1A]. The Havana Docks matter names NCLH as defendant, was remanded to the Eleventh Circuit in June 2026 and is “reasonably possible but not probable” with no liability recorded; whether NCLC bears it is not stated [Q3 10-Q page:22] (Insufficient Information).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Liquidity and near-term maturities: cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million against USD 238.6 million of scheduled principal for the rest of 2026, with the revolver upsized after quarter-end (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Funding model: most new ships are financed by long-dated fixed-rate export-credit loans, such as the 1.91% term loan maturing February 25, 2038 for Norwegian Luna, and about USD 10.8 billion of committed undrawn facilities remain (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:42). (3) Fixed-rate profile: 88% of debt is fixed, so base-rate moves affect a small part of interest cost (Documentary Fact; Q3 10-Q page:43). (4) Parent support and no leakage: NCLH contributed equity proceeds in 2025 and no distributions to the parent appear in the periods read (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (5) Operating cash flow of USD 1,709.3 million for nine months 2026 and seasonally strong third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.8% (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (6) Management cost and fleet actions, including run-rate savings programs and ship charters and sales, are described and under way, but are Management Language until they show in results (Management Language; CP-1A).

Weaknesses. (1) Leverage of 5.51x total and 5.42x net, higher than at FY2025 (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Negative post-capex cash flow of USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 and growth spending financed by debt (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (3) Earnings and yield softness: Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA down 8.1%, Net Yield lower, and a booked position that management says remains below its optimal range (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (4) Springing revolver maturity on November 17, 2026 with an undefined liquidity test (Insufficient Information; 10-K page:142). (5) Concentrated maturities in 2030 and an unfinanced part of the newbuild program (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:41). (6) Currency exposure on unhedged euro payments and debt (Documentary Fact; Q3 10-Q page:44). (7) Demand concentration: about 84% of revenue from U.S.-sourced guests and customer deposits that are partly refundable (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (8) Evidence gaps: no agreements, no covenant values, a reduced-disclosure annual report and a perimeter difference between the issuer's filings and the parent's releases (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A).

| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Springing revolver maturity on November 17, 2026 | The clause accelerates the revolver if the 2027 exchangeable notes are not repaid or refinanced and a liquidity test is not met; the test and the amendment's effect are not supplied. | Loss of the main backstop would force reliance on cash of USD 250.7 million; cross-default and collateral consequences follow. | Material |

| High and rising leverage with softer earnings | Debt rose while Adjusted EBITDA fell, and yield per Capacity Day is lower. | Little cushion for further earnings decline before covenant or rating pressure; ratings are B1 and B+ per the filing. | Material |

| Negative post-capex cash flow | Operating cash flow did not cover additions to property and equipment for nine months 2026. | Debt grows with each delivery; deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth. | Material |

| Unfinanced newbuild contracts and euro exposure | Three effective contracts are not yet financed; EUR 14.1 billion of payments are unhedged. | Future funding need and dollar cost uncertainty. | Material |
| 2030 maturity concentration | USD 4,134.3 million of scheduled principal falls in 2030. | Refinancing depends on market access and ratings. | Material |
| Covenant opacity | Covenant values, definitions and the October 2026 amendment are not supplied. | Headroom cannot be monitored. | Material |
| Demand concentration and refundable deposits | About 84% of revenue from U.S.-sourced guests; customer deposits are partly refundable. | A booking shock would drain liquidity quickly. | Material |
| Parent linkage and share-price exposure of the exchangeable notes | Notes exchange into NCLH shares; NCLH guarantees them. | Settlement and support depend on the parent. | Minor |
| Contingent litigation and unfunded pension | Havana Docks exposure and the Shipboard Retirement Plan are not quantified for NCLC. | Possible claims outside debt. | Minor |

## Calculations
All inputs are as printed in US$ thousands, millions or billions; amounts in prose are converted to USD millions.
### Liquidity
- Liquidity at September 30, 2026: cash 250.7 + revolver availability about 1,100 = about 1,350.7. The filing states about 1.4 billion (Q3 10-Q page:6).
- Implied revolver use: commitments about 2,500 − availability about 1,100 = about 1,400. This includes any letters of credit and is derived from rounded figures.

- Pro forma availability after October 2026: about 1,100 + commitment increase about 300 (2,800 − 2,500) + repayment 380.0 = about 1,780, consistent with the parent's 1.8 billion; pro forma cash for the issuer is Not supplied.

- Cash against the free-liquidity minimum: cash 179.2 (March 31, 2026) and 212.3 (June 30, 2026) are below 250 (10-K page:41); cash 250.7 at September 30, 2026 is above it; the covenant definition is not supplied.
### Funding of 2027 needs

- 2027 anticipated ship construction and growth spending 3.1 billion − export-credit funding 2.0 billion = 1.1 billion unfunded (Q3 10-Q page:40). Rest of 2026: 1.1 billion − 0.6 billion = 0.5 billion, plus 0.1 billion of other capital expenditure. 2028: 1.8 billion − 1.3 billion = 0.5 billion.

- 2027 unfunded spending 1,100 + scheduled principal 1,105.7 = 2,205.7; against LTM operating cash flow 2,169.0 (CP-1) the ratio is 2,205.7 / 2,169.0 = 1.02x. Illustrative: uses printed rounded plans and a trailing cash flow, not a forecast.
### Maturity and structure shares

- December 31, 2025 composition of USD 14,583.4 million of debt: senior unsecured notes 5,237.6 (35.9%), exchangeable notes 1,925.1 (13.2%), revolver 1,100.0 (7.5%), export-credit and term loans 6,312.1 (43.3%), finance leases 8.7 (0.1%). Sum of the 29 rows equals 14,583.4 (10-K page:140). Shares calculated; they total 100.0% within rounding.

- Variable-rate debt implied by the sensitivity: 18.2 / 1% = about 1,820, which is about 12% of 14,884.5, consistent with the stated 12% (Q3 10-Q page:43). The one percentage point rise adds 18.2 / 753.1 = 2.4% to LTM interest expense, net (CP-1).
### Pro forma maturity buckets (illustrative)
- 2028: 1,346.1 − 525.0 = 821.1 (assumes the full principal named in the 10-K debt table was outstanding at September 30, 2026; the Q3 10-Q does not state the amount redeemed).
- 2030: 4,134.3 − 380.0 = 3,754.3 (assumes the revolver is shown at its 2030 maturity in the schedule, as the 10-K schedule appears to do).
- 2031: 1,875.1 + 950.0 = 2,825.1. The USD 42.2 million of export-credit prepayment is not allocated to a year.
### Interest change net of extinguishment
- 9M 2025 interest expense, net 782.4 − extinguishment 202.5 = 579.9; 9M 2026 564.5 / 579.9 − 1 = −2.7% (CP-1).
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| The Revolving Loan Facility credit agreement, its liquidity test, the third amendment and the effect on the November 17, 2026 springing maturity are not supplied. | High | CP-5 and committee | Obtain the agreement and amendment; confirm whether the 2027 exchangeable notes are repaid or refinanced before November 17, 2026. |
| Covenant ratio values, covenant EBITDA and free liquidity definitions are not supplied; headroom is Not calculable. | High | CP-5 | Obtain the compliance certificate and agreement definitions. |

| The instrument-level debt table at September 30, 2026 and the security and guarantors by instrument are not supplied. | Medium | CP-5 | Rebuild from the December 31, 2025 table and the described 2026 events, flagged as derived. |
| The revolver drawn amount, letters of credit and the issuer's pro forma cash after October 2026 are not supplied. | Medium | CP-5 | Use stated availability and label the pro forma as calculated. |
| Parent and issuer debt totals and net leverage do not reconcile in the supplied text; the parent's 5.5x is not used. | Medium | CP-5 | Keep perimeters separate. |
| Governance, beneficial ownership and executive compensation are omitted by the reduced-disclosure annual report. | Medium | CP-5 | Look to parent filings; treat as parent-level. |
| Pension obligation amount and the issuer's share of the Havana Docks exposure are not quantified. | Low | CP-5 | Carry as outside-debt items. |
| Events between October 29, 2026 and 2026-11-05 are Not supplied; for example whether the 2027 exchangeable notes were repaid early. | Low | All | State as Not supplied. |
| Text extraction was not compared with the filed HTML or XBRL. | Low | CP-5 | Re-check figures that drive a conclusion. |
## Next module

CP-5 should run next to trace every material claim here to its source page and to check consistency across CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A and this answer. Carry forward: the issuer-only perimeter, the springing revolver maturity of November 17, 2026 and its linkage to the February 15, 2027 exchangeable notes, the missing agreements and covenant values, the unfinanced newbuild contracts and the derived (not printed) status of the 2027 funding ratio, pro forma availability and maturity shares.

## Calculations

All inputs in USD millions unless thousands are stated, taken from the cited pages or from CP-1 and CP-2. Every upstream derived number was recomputed; the results are in T5B.5. New calculations made in this audit:

- Revolver clause (a) test: the 10-K table title gives USD 600.0 million for the 7.75% senior unsecured notes due 2029 (10-K page:140); 600.0 exceeds the USD 400 million threshold, so the notes qualify if outstanding and not refinanced beyond April 23, 2030. The 6.125% notes due 2028 (USD 525.0 million) also exceeded it and were redeemed from the October 2026 proceeds (S4 page:11). The exact 2029 maturity date is not in the pages read, so the trigger date is Not calculable.
- Pension: current portion 1.9 + non-current 32.8 = 34.7, equal to the projected benefit obligation of 34,729 thousand (10-K page:159).

- Advance ticket sales: 3,200,593 / 3,105,964 - 1 = +3.0 percent (December 2025 against December 2024); 3,141,976 / 3,200,593 - 1 = -1.8 percent (September 30, 2026 against December 31, 2025). Quarterly balances from CP-1: 3,718.9 at March 31, 3,651.2 at June 30 and 3,142.0 at September 30, 2026.
- Sale of ships: proceeds 104,995 thousand in nine months 2026 and loss on disposal 16,825 thousand (S4 page:3, page:7).
